claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by the interplay between dislocation accumulation and dynamic recovery.
Low temperatures limit dynamic recovery in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
High strain rates promote pronounced dislocation pile-ups in Co-free FeNiCrMn when dynamic recovery is limited.
Pronounced dislocation pile-ups increase the yield strength of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Higher temperatures enhance dynamic recovery in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Enhanced dynamic recovery reduces dislocation buildup and promotes ductility.
The proposed specimens are Co-free FeNiCrMn produced by conventional casting followed by homogenization.
Dynamic compression testing will span 77 K to 300 K.
Compression testing will span quasi-static strain rates below 10^-3 s^-1 through high strain rates above 10^2 s^-1.
Restricted diffusion at low temperature limits dynamic recovery.
Higher dislocation densities and pile-up prevalence will correlate with increased yield strength under low-temperature, high-strain-rate loading.
At higher temperatures, fewer dislocation pile-ups will correlate with improved ductility.
In situ synchrotron or neutron diffraction can quantify dislocation-density evolution and changes in dislocation configurations during the proposed tests.
Post-mortem TEM can distinguish dislocation pile-ups from other microstructural features.
The proposed mechanism may not apply after substantial changes in processing, grain size, or composition.
Failure to find a consistent relationship between dislocation density or pile-ups and mechanical response would falsify the hypothesis.
A stronger relationship of deformation twinning or grain-boundary effects with mechanical response would falsify the proposed dislocation-recovery mechanism.
